<!-- pr-reviewer: 279ac89f1cdab681655ad8559f1cc2ad74e71836 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** The approach is right and well bounded, but there are two ways the mesh reading clears a fixture that is really in the carried part. The old box check refused both. This is a collision law, so every way it can clear has to be correct and pinned.

### What looks good
- Box first, then mesh, and the mesh can only clear. The `scan` refactor keeps `penetration` the same, and `carried_fixtures_cache` passes unchanged.
- "Closed" is a real check: `FixtureMesh::build` refuses unpaired or misoriented edges (`MeshError::Open`), and a refused mesh keeps the box depth. I checked this with an open-sheet soft-jaw probe: refused, 5.00 mm.
- Budget exhaustion is never read as a partial answer: `crossings` marks the line ambiguous and `steel_on_line` returns `None`. The sim test pins this (mutation M4 below).
- Frames: `world_facets` and `entity_world_aabb` use the same world transform, so the mesh is read in the same frame as the old box. The FlipX pins cover the flipped case.
- Numeric safety: no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`. Non-finite input returns `None`. NaN-safe `total_cmp`. Flat facets are skipped, and `n`/`u`/`v` that are not finite count as ambiguous.
- The column skip only drops columns whose box depth cannot beat the worst depth found so far. Mesh depth is at most box depth, so the verdict and depth stay the same.
- Repo rules: provenance comments (Haines, O'Rourke, Ericson), files well under 400 lines, a decision record, a `Changelog:` line, `Fixes #1530`, a conventional subject. No snapshot, golden or `CHANGELOG.md` edits, and no process files, so no `PROCESS_VERSION` bump is needed.

### Local results (trial-merged with main 8bbac739, clean merge)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| sim lib | 146 passed |
| sim fixture_mesh_column | 6 passed |
| sim fixture_mesh_convict / fixture_mesh_posed / posed_band_cylinder | 5 / 9 (1 ignored) / 3 passed |
| app lib | 194 passed |
| app carried_fixture_shape | 7 passed |
| app carried_fixtures_cache, fixture_mesh, fixture_mesh_posed, fixtures, builtin_vise, fixture_law_gaps, posting, setup_carry, setup_mount | 7, 3, 2, 14, 9, 3, 17, 9, 6 passed |
| clippy `-p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings` | clean |
| clippy `-p camcraft-sim` (lib + `fixture_mesh_column`) | clean. `--all-targets` stops on a lint that is already on main in `crates/sim/tests/fixture_mesh_convict.rs:152` (`needless_range_loop`), a file this PR does not touch |
| Release timing: a 400 k-facet fan, burning the 50 M-visit budget on lines through the fan centre | 0.52 s (the claimed 0.39 s, same order) |

### Mutation table (each restored afterwards; sim and app fixture suites run)
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| M1 drop the closed-mesh check (`build`) | red: `fixture_mesh::the_same_vise_as_an_open_sheet_keeps_the_box_verdict`. That test pins the #339 path, not this clause |
| M2 refused mesh clears (`Err(why) => None`, fixture_carried.rs:202) | **green: unpinned** |
| M3 unread line / spent budget clears (`map_or(boxed, ..)` -> `map_or(0.0, ..)`, :172) | **green: unpinned** |
| M4 spent budget reads a partial line (column.rs) | red: `a_spent_budget_reads_nothing_and_never_guesses` |
| M5 centre line only, no side lines (:171) | green. This makes the check stricter, not looser, but the PR's own mutation table, which lists it as red, is out of date |
| M6 sub-cell footprint clears | red: `a_fixture_narrower_than_a_cell_is_judged_by_the_column_under_it` |
| M7 coarse-fidelity fixture judged by its mesh (:189) | **green: unpinned** |
| M8 parity rule dropped, positive winding only (column.rs:130) | **green: unpinned** |
| M9 tolerance subtracted from depth | red: 4 pins |
| M10 edge/vertex hit not treated as ambiguous | red: `a_line_on_a_facet_diagonal_is_nudged_off_it_and_read` |

### Requested before merge
1. **A fixture feature narrower than the column pitch clears (safety).** Each column is read only on its centre line and four lines 0.01 mm beside it (`crates/app/src/fixture_carried.rs:171`). Steel that stands between two columns' lines is never seen. On this PR's own `flipped_hat` (pitch 0.375 mm), the clear nest from `soft_jaws(.., 25.05, 0.0)` was probed with two features standing into the part, each placed on a column boundary:
   - a 0.19 x 0.19 mm post, Z 0..3 (3 mm into the part): **no refusal**;
   - a 0.19 mm x 50 mm lip, Z 0..4 (4 mm into the part, along Y at x ≈ 10): **no refusal**.

   On main, the box refuses both. The pitch is `max(r/8, span/1023)` (`sim::stock_sim::cut::auto_cell`), so on a 1 m stock a feature up to about 1 mm (a dowel tip, a jaw lip or serration) passes the same way. The decision record covers only "an overlap narrower than half a cell beside a face". A feature that lies wholly between columns is a new hole, and the old box check did not have it.

   Please refuse it, then pin it with the post and the lip. One way: before the mesh may clear a fixture, check the mesh's own geometry against the material. For example, keep the box depth when any mesh vertex, or any facet whose XY extent is narrower than the pitch, stands more than `CARRIED_CONTACT_TOL` inside a column's material. Another way: read lines across the whole cell area, not only its centre. Whatever the rule, a feature narrower than the pitch must not clear.
2. **An inside-out shell that overlaps another shell reads its steel as air.** `spans_of` (`crates/sim/src/fixture_mesh/column.rs:130`) keeps steel only where the winding is nonzero or the crossing count is odd. Take two closed shells, A at Z 0..10 and B at Z 5..15 with its facets reversed. Edge pairing accepts this mesh as closed. The line reads `[(0,5),(10,15)]`, so the steel at 5..10 is cleared. An imported multi-body STL with one body flipped is enough to cause it.

   Please return `None` (keep the box) when the winding goes negative on a line, or does not end at 0 with an even count. Pin it with that two-shell mesh. Mutation M8 is unpinned today.
3. **Pin the remaining clearing paths at app level.** M2, M3 and M7 are green:
   - an open or refused mesh in the carried clause keeps the box depth (e.g. the soft jaws with one facet removed -> `5.00 mm deep`);
   - an unread line or a spent budget keeps the box depth (`mesh_penetration` is `pub` and takes the budget, so a call with `budget = 0` should give back `penetration(body, b)`);
   - a coarse-fidelity fixture (#864) keeps the box depth.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- `nudge_unit` is 1e-6 x the largest absolute coordinate. That includes the fixture's distance from the origin, not only its size. I placed a 6 µm-wide block at X 5000 and read a line on its top-face diagonal. The line was nudged ~19 µm, off the block, and read `Some([])`. Within about 2 m of the origin the largest nudge (~5.5 µm) stays below the 0.01 mm tolerance. Capping it, e.g. at `CARRIED_CONTACT_TOL / 10`, would make that hold everywhere.
- A rotated (not flipped) setup is not pinned. The frame code is shared with the box, so I expect it holds; one pin would make sure.
- The `FixtureMesh` is rebuilt on every gate call. That is fine at the measured costs. Just noting it in case the clause later runs per frame.
- The PR's mutation table says "centre line only" turns red. With the scaled nudge it is now green (M5 above); please update the table.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 87f657fa03880439070510439d5328e40a87d13a -->
**Needs changes before merge.** This is a small, test-sized change. The rework fixes both blockers from the last review. Whole-rectangle reading between the columns is a sound rule, and every probe that cleared before is now refused. One thing is left: the new rectangle path's contact band is not pinned. Two mutations that widen it stay green, and below a 0.02 mm pitch the code skips the band where its comment says the box is kept. Ruling on the one-pitch limit: it is already on main, it does not block this PR, and it is bounded (see below).

### What looks good
- `steel_in_prism` (`crates/sim/src/fixture_mesh/prism.rs`) is correct as argued. Each facet is clipped to the rectangle, and Z is linear on the convex clipped polygon, so `hi > a && lo < b` really does mean a surface point lies in the slab. With no facet over the rectangle there is no steel. A slab that holds no surface is decided by one line. Unread, non-finite and inverted input all give `Unread`, and the caller turns that into the box depth (`fixture_carried.rs:253`).
- `spans_of` now refuses negative winding and keeps the box (`column.rs:138`). A wholly inside-out mesh also reads `None`, so it is safe in both directions.
- The nudge cap holds whatever the coordinates are (`NUDGE_CAP`, `column.rs:43`).
- Every app-level clearing path from the last review is now pinned (table below).
- Repo rules: provenance is on `prism.rs` (Sutherland-Hodgman, O'Rourke). Files: `fixture_carried.rs` 325 lines, `prism.rs` 139, `column.rs` 182, all under 400. The decision record and PR body are updated, the `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #1530` are there, the commit subjects are conventional, and there are no snapshot, golden, `CHANGELOG.md` or process-file edits.

### Local results (trial-merged with upstream main f402b368, clean merge)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| sim lib | 146 passed |
| sim fixture_mesh_column | 12 passed |
| sim fixture_mesh_convict / fixture_mesh_posed / posed_band_cylinder | 5 / 9 (1 ignored) / 3 passed |
| app lib | 204 passed |
| app carried_fixture_shape / carried_fixture_guards | 11 / 5 passed |
| app carried_fixtures_cache, fixture_mesh, fixture_mesh_posed, fixtures, builtin_vise, fixture_law_gaps, posting, setup_carry, setup_mount, accessory_collisions, verify | 7, 3, 2, 14, 9, 3, 17, 9, 6, 2, 21 (2 ignored) passed |
| clippy `-p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings` | clean |
| clippy `-p camcraft-sim --lib --test fixture_mesh_column --test fixture_mesh_posed --test fixture_mesh` | clean. `--all-targets` still stops on main's own lint at `crates/sim/tests/fixture_mesh_convict.rs:152`, which this PR does not touch |

**The last review's probes, on this head:**
- the 0.19 x 0.19 post 3 mm in, at 36 positions across one cell of the flipped hat: refused 36/36;
- the 0.19 mm lip 4 mm in, at 8 phases across the cell: refused 8/8;
- the inside-out shell overlapping another: `None`, so the box stands (pinned);
- the 6 µm block at X 5000: read where it stands (pinned).

**Release timing (M-series Mac).** The fixture is a 100 k-segment cylinder (400 k facets) whose top cap lies in contact with the material. A tall block off the grid makes its box flag every column and rectangle near the fan centre.
- With the budget: 0.80 s when the mesh clears, 0.74 s when it penetrates at the last column. Both use the 50 M visits and keep the box verdict.
- With no limit: 7.1 s / 6.2 s (146 M visits).

These are the same order as the 0.34 s you report. The budget bounds the time as claimed.

### Ruling on the one-pitch limit at a side face or step
I measured main's box law (`penetration`, which this PR leaves unchanged) and this head on the same carried bodies.

- **Hand-built body, pitch 1.0.** A single box jaw (its box is its mesh) overlaps the part's side face by 0.9 pitch, at 11 phases of the face against the grid.
  - Main and this head agree at every phase: 10 refusals at 6.00 mm, and 1 pass. The pass is where the material column's centre lies exactly on the jaw face, and both let it through.
  - Add a second jaw on the far side, so the box spans the part like a vise. Main refuses 11/11 and this head 10/11.
  - Main's eleventh refusal is the #1530 false positive: main also refuses that vise at a 0.1-pitch overlap, and at zero.
- **The flipped hat, pitch 0.375.** The nearest material column centre is 24.6875, which is 0.83 pitch inside the face at X 25.
  - A single jaw overlapping by 0.1, 0.3, 0.5 or 0.7 pitch: main and this head both pass.
  - At 0.9, 1.0, 1.2 or 1.5 pitch: both refuse, `5.00 mm deep`. The gate gives the same lines.

**Ruling: this is a limit that is already on main, not a new loosening, and it does not block this PR.**
- For any fixture whose box is its shape, the side-face verdict is identical to main's at every phase. The resolution is set by the carried dexel's column centres, and the box law had exactly the same blind band.
- Only an over-wide box, a vise spanning the part, is refused by main and cleared here inside the band. That refusal was the bug #1530 fixes, because main refused the same vise at a correct grip too.
- **It is bounded by construction to under one pitch:**
  - steel more than one pitch inside a face either covers a material column's lines, which `on_columns` reads, or lies in a rectangle of four material columns, which is read whole;
  - only rectangles touching an empty column, or the part of a step that the four corners do not share, go unread, and both lie within one cell of the boundary.
  - On the shipped grid that is 0.375 mm on the test stock, and about 1 mm on 1 m stock (`max(r/8, span/1023)`).

It is documented in the decision record. Two follow-ups, neither blocking:
- **Wording.** "it lies within a cell of a material boundary, never inside the material" should say "at most one pitch into the material at a side face or step": the steel that passes is inside the part, by less than one pitch.
- **Its own issue.** I found none filed. Please file it (`P7`, `area:sim`, `source:agent`, "Done means: side-face contact resolved finer than one pitch, or the bound pinned at several phases"), and link it from the decision record.

### Requested before merge
1. **Pin the rectangle path's contact band with literals** (P2b and P2c are green). The column path is pinned at 0.03 / 0.005 mm. The rectangle path uses its own call-site trims (`fixture_carried.rs:242` and `:249`), and widening either one threefold still passes every pin. Two hand-built pins in `carried_fixture_guards.rs` close this. On a 3 x 3 body (1 mm pitch, material Z 0..10, with a plate under it at Z -5..0), I checked both on this head:
   - a sub-pitch block 0.03 mm tall mid-cell, `(0.9, 0.9, 0) .. (1.1, 1.1, 0.03)`, is refused `Some(0.03)`, while the same block 0.005 mm tall is held `None`. This turns P2b red;
   - a 0.015 mm post just off a column's side line, `(1.512, 0.9, 0) .. (1.527, 1.1, 3)`, is refused `Some(3.0)`. This turns P2c red.
2. **Below a 0.02 mm pitch, the box is not kept, although the comment says it is** (`fixture_carried.rs:242-249`). When `cell < 2 * CARRIED_CONTACT_TOL`, the trimmed rectangle is inverted (`x0 > x1`). The off-footprint test at `:243` then returns `continue` ("no steel") before the `slim` branch is reached, but the comment at `:246` says a rectangle too slim to read keeps the box. Probe: a carried body with a 0.015 mm pitch (a 0.3 mm tool on a 20 mm part reaches this) and a 0.003 x 0.003 mm post 3 mm into the material between the column lines. Main's box refuses it at 3.0. This head clears it (`None`). The steel is narrower than 2 x tol, so it is tiny, but the code should do what its comment says. Please test `slim` (or `x0 > x1`) before the off-footprint `continue`, and pin it with that probe (it also makes P5 red).

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- **A strip of 2 x tol around each column line is not read.** The 5 lines sit at the centre and ±0.01 mm, and the rectangles start at +0.01 mm. So a wall narrower than 0.02 mm lying along a column line passes. On the hat, a lip 0.015 or 0.019 mm wide on a column line, 4 mm into the part, is held; at 0.021 mm it is refused, `4.00 mm deep`. This is the contact-tolerance design (a face on a centre line is contact), and it is bounded by 2 x `CARRIED_CONTACT_TOL`. One sentence in the decision record would make it explicit.
- G2 and P10 stay green for the reasons in the table. That is fine as it stands.
- A rotated (not flipped) setup is still not pinned. The frame code is shared with the box, so this is low risk.
- The budgeted worst case on my construction is 0.74-0.80 s, not 0.34 s. Both are bounded and below a second; the difference is just the fixture used.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
